question: Is OpenAI's upcoming "Astra" model going to be called GPT-6?
resolution_criteria:
OpenAI is reportedly not sure between calling it GPT-6 and GPT-5.7

To be clear, "GPT-6 Astra" as a name would meet the YES requirement
research:
## 1. Resolution source
- No official resolution URL is given. The question appears to come from a Manifold market, "Is OpenAI's upcoming Astra model going to be called GPT-6?" The text says "GPT-6 Astra" counts as YES. It in practice resolves on the name OpenAI uses when it officially releases the model. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/BenjaminShindel/is-openais-upcoming-astra-model-goi), [copy](https://manifold.markets/Bayesian/is-openais-upcoming-astra-model-goi)
- I could not fetch the market pages because the proxy refused the connection, so I can't report the live probability. Search snippets showed two copies of the market at about 31% and about 42%, both closing Dec 31. The snapshot dates are unknown.
- As of 2026-08-25, OpenAI had not officially announced a product name. "Astra" is its own label for the model.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settled the question by 2026-08-25. The reporting says OpenAI had not chosen between GPT-6, GPT-5.7 or another name. [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/artificial-intelligence/openai-teases-astra-its-next-major-ai-model-after-it-solves-10-long-standing-math-problems/)
- The current lineup is GPT-5.5 (released 2026-04-23) followed by GPT-5.6 (Sol/Terra/Luna tiers). That makes "5.7" the natural next step and "6" a jump to a new generation. [Wikipedia GPT-5.5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-5.5)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- About 2026-08-18: a widely shared X summary repeated that OpenAI calls Astra its "next major model" and that the name is unconfirmed. [VraserX on X](https://x.com/VraserX/status/2089780798027112737)
- August 2026 (exact date not found): The Information confirmed Astra is a new model family built for long-running, multi-agent workloads. Secondary coverage says the report described the naming as undecided between GPT-6, GPT-5.7 or something else. I could not find The Information's original article. [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/artificial-intelligence/openai-teases-astra-its-next-major-ai-model-after-it-solves-10-long-standing-math-problems/)
- Several pre-launch blogs (for example Geeky Gadgets) called the model "GPT-5.7 Astra" and said "ChatGPT 6" would be a separate model codenamed "Doug." Some secondary sources also mention an unverified GPT-6 base model codenamed "Bel." These sources are low-reliability. [Geeky Gadgets](https://www.geeky-gadgets.com/openai-chatgpt-6-doug-astra/)
- 2026-08-07: Axios exclusive. OpenAI "cannot rule out" that Astra has "Critical" cyber capabilities under its Preparedness Framework, so it is slowing the release and expanding safety testing. Altman said OpenAI wants Astra to be generally available but needs "a little bit longer." [Axios](https://axios.com/2026/08/07/openai-astra-model-delay-cybersecurity-risks), [Engadget](https://engadget.com/2233237/openai-slows-down-astra-development-due-to-cybersecurity-concerns)
- 2026-08-01/02: OpenAI's research post called Astra "our next major model." An internal version produced results on 10 long-open math and theoretical computer science problems, published with Lean 4 proofs. The post gave no product name, release date or API ID. [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/02/openais-astra-solves-10-long-open-math-problems-publishes-proofs/), [The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/openai-astra-model-ten-math-proofs-non-sofic-groups)

## 4. Base rates
- OpenAI has a record of avoiding the next whole number and using point releases instead. Its GPT-4 era went through GPT-4o, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.5 before GPT-5. In 2025-2026 it has shipped GPT-5.1 through 5.6 roughly every 1 to 2 months. [Wikipedia GPT-4.5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-4.5), [Wikipedia GPT-5.4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-5.4)
- The case for a new generation number: OpenAI itself says "next major model," calls Astra a "new model family," and its cyber capability is a step change (first possible "Critical" rating). OpenAI has also used codenames for products before (for example "Orion" became GPT-4.5 rather than GPT-5).
- I found no clear base rate for "codenamed model ships under a whole new number." Historically, OpenAI has usually chosen the more conservative label.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Manifold naming market (this question): about 31% and about 42% on two copies. The dates of these readings are unknown. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/BenjaminShindel/is-openais-upcoming-astra-model-goi)
- Polymarket "GPT-6 released by…" markets. These require the "GPT-6" label, and "GPT-5.5 or similar" does not count:
  - Dec 31, 2026 contract: 84¢ in mid-April and about 87% on 2026-07-20.
  - Aug 31 contract: about 71% on 2026-07-20.
  - Sept 15 contract: about 21% in mid-August.
  [CryptoSlate](https://cryptoslate.com/predictions/market/gpt-6-released-by/), [Orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/will-gpt-6-be-released-by-september-15-2026)
- Polymarket "Astra released by Aug 31" (counts any model named Astra): about 78% (about 70.5% on some aggregators) on 2026-08-07. The roughly 57-point gap between this and the GPT-6 market suggests traders thought an Astra launch would likely not carry the GPT-6 label. [Pillitteri](https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/10089/polymarket-astra-78-percent-august)
- Manifold "GPT-6 released by Sept 15": about 18%. "By Oct 31": about 48%. Both are undated snapshots. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/event/will-gpt-6-be-released-by-september)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (around 2026-09-05)
- An official Astra launch announcement or blog post would settle the name. The Axios slowdown points to a launch after cyber safeguards are ready, and no date had been announced as of 2026-08-25.
- Other signals to watch:
  - model ID strings showing up in the API, Codex or ChatGPT client code ("gpt-6-…" vs "gpt-5.7-…")
  - a published system card
  - further reporting from The Information or Axios on the naming
  - Altman posts on X
- If the release slips past the resolution window, the market may stay open (the Manifold copies close Dec 31).

**Caveat:** Many search results were dated after 2026-08-25. I ignored them as the exercise requires. Several page fetches failed, so some dates above come from search snippets.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- **No:** Astra launches in September as "GPT-5.7" with agentic features, and GPT-6 is reserved for a later base model. Alternatively, the launch slips past the window with no name.
- **Yes:** OpenAI uses Astra's math and agent breakthroughs to brand a generational jump and launches it as "GPT-6" once the cyber safeguards clear.

**(f) Moving to a final number.** I start from a base rate of about 33% and use the Manifold markets on this same question (31-42%) as an anchor. I adjust slightly upward because of the "next major model" and "new model family" language. I then adjust downward because of the short resolution window, the safety delay and the low "GPT-6 by Sept 15" price. The net result is about 35%.

Probability: 35%
